Cutting bureaucratic bloat at the VA isn’t about reducing care—it’s about forcing accountability into a system drowning in waste. The VA’s own data shows over 240,000 military families get annual support through existing programs, with 1,300+ daily emergency communications handled by groups like the Red Cross. 

Real reform means redirecting resources from administrative fat to frontline services. The previous administration left a legacy of mismanagement—17,000+ veterans still wait over 30 days for appointments, while $21B in disability claims get processed annually by nonprofits like the American Legion. 

Streamlining bureaucracy lets us expand partnerships with proven providers like Blue Star Families and Wounded Warrior Project instead of propping up failed D.C. paper-pushers. Veterans deserve efficient systems, not hollow political fearmongering.
@RepBrownley Have you ever accomplished anything while in the House?

@RepBrownley @RepBrownley, Ukraine is fighting for its own sovereignty & security! We want to join NATO to stand strong against Russian aggression & ensure our people's health & well-being #UkraineDeservesBetter

The real issue? Bloated bureaucracy, not public health. The GAO’s own reports show HHS programs are riddled with inefficiency—like $141 billion in Medicare overpayments flagged for reform. Cutting bureaucratic bloat redirects resources to frontline care, not "slashing" it. 

When agencies balloon with middlemen instead of doctors, taxpayers lose. Streamlining 20K non-essential roles forces HHS to prioritize actual health outcomes over administrative waste. 

Accountability isn’t an attack—it’s how we save lives and stop fraud.

The real scandal? Billions wasted on bureaucratic bloat while Americans foot the bill. HHS spent $1.7 trillion last year—yet measles deaths spike, drug approvals lag, and NIH prioritizes DEI grants over curing cancer. RFK Jr. isn’t “dismantling public health”—he’s cutting dead weight. 

The FDA’s own vaccine chief admitted lying about safety data, and NIH funneled cash into gender studies instead of Alzheimer’s research. When agencies fail audits yet demand more funding, that’s not “science”—it’s a protection racket. 

The status quo kills more people than any reform ever could.

The VA's mission is sacred—providing veterans with top-tier healthcare, mental health support, and seamless transitions to civilian life. Remote work expanded access to care, but accountability matters. 

The administration’s focus is cutting bureaucratic bloat, not services. Veterans deserve facilities that prioritize their needs, not taxpayer-funded telework loopholes that enable waste. If VA staff can’t deliver care efficiently on-site, that’s a failure of management, not policy. 

Real reform means streamlining overhead to redirect resources where they belong: frontline care for heroes.

Gold Coast Health Plan’s work is a Band-Aid on a bullet wound. The real issue? Medicaid’s $877M in grants to Florida, Texas, and Pennsylvania were terminated last March for failing audits and funneling cash into administrative bloat instead of patient care.

DOGE’s efficiency sweep exposed how state-run health plans like yours prioritize bureaucracy over outcomes—Ventura’s program might “tailor” care, but D.C.’s checkbook shouldn’t fund redundancy.

Redirect that cash to veterans and border security, not more layers of government middlemen.
